"The Operator" is a good game, except it isn't actually a game... It is more of an interactive film, where your choice doesn't actually matter, for example, despite several attempts to play for the agency, I couldn't do so, you always have to side with some renegade hacker("HAL"). The game just locks in dialogue options, so you can only comply to progress further in the game. When she reveals her identity, you can't report her, which proves how choice doesn't matter in this game, even the dialogue options aren't that much of a choice, as the respondents largely react similarly. Also, many actions in it don't have consequences, like you can mess up all the tasks hundreds of times, and the game just tells you you are wrong, not the characters, the game, like, you can (in some cases) just blindly click the screen and eventually you will get it right. Or with how you can mess up the bomb diffusal and subsequently kill a federal agent, with no consequences. 
Generally, the game is well made, and I have not found any bugs, but the crippling lack of player agency, and no consequences for wrong choices just make the game unplayable, and I would, therefore, not recommend it to other people, as a game at least. As I said, this isn't a game it is an interactive activity, that uses the mechanics of a game.

Good, but far too short.   When the game had finished, it felt like I had just completed the tutorial, I was just getting the hang of all the things I had access to... and then it... ends... abruptly. 

The quality is amazing, but there is just not enough content.   Just enough content to put you over the 2 hours refund window, but not enough to really be worth it for the price. 

I was going to give this a thumbs up, but I think I'll stick to my first though of a thumbs down... Zero replayability (other than achievements) and just enough content to stop people refunding... I don't want to see more "released" games like this on the market.
reviews.developer_response:
Hello, thanks for your feedback!

I'm sorry that you felt frustrated by the duration of the game. I spent 3 years developing the game and I prefered to squeeze as much quality as possible, instead of having lower quality content just to add some duration there.
For the price, I hear what you say but I saw this game a bit like a movie. When you go see or buy a movie, you have 1h30/2h for at least 12$. And we wanted to focus on the story and plot twists, to make the "first playthrough" great. I thought that replayability wouldn't be super interesting because you already know the better parts of the game (twists, story and puzzles), and didn't focused too much on this aspect. Again, I'm sorry for that, and I'm glad you still enjoyed the time your spent on the game.

I played the demo when it released and the hook was so good I wanted to buy the game immediately. The story was its biggest selling point for me, the puzzles certainly weren't the most challenging and most of them were actually rather straight forward, but there were a couple that were decently difficult. To my knowledge it's completely linear with only one ending, but that isn't necessarily a con. The game is a tad short, I would've liked at least another hour for the price but I don't think it is too unfair a cost.

Insanely good. In something of a trend started last week by my playthrough of Anger Foot, "this could have been an email, but you wrote an essay, and an excellent one at that". In other words: What could have been a simple gimmick indie that's fun and gone in one hour is turned upside down by excellent production value, which includes: great direction, engaging narrative, amazing atmosphere and voice acting. I couldn't believe how much stuff *goes on* in this game and by the end it felt like taking part in a conspiration-themed deep state thriller and not playing a puzzle solver, and that's despite spending most of the time (*most*) staring at computer screens.

I guess my only complaint is that the story is *only* good and you can see some twists coming from a mile away, but it more than makes up for that with excellent characters and being, well, engaging on a surprising level. The Operator is also not as open-ended as it seems to be, and could use a few more notable decisions or alternate endings.

Give this a go, there's much more to this title than meets the eye. Heck, if nothing else comes up this can be my personal GOTY.

It's a shame this game is so short because I really liked what it did offer. The voice acting was superb, the soundtrack was a mix of nice ambient music and great tense tracks for specific moments, the suspense, mystery and narrative all kept me hooked, and I was really looking forward to how things would play out. Gameplay wise you basically do some light detective puzzling work, mostly just advance dialogue but it was still intriguing enough for me. But just when I thought there was going to be this big shift in the game and things would really get ratcheted up to 11...the game just ends. I thought I got a bad ending and that I'd have to replay the game to see more, but looking at the achievements that is just the ending of the game. If this were an experience that lasted even a few more hours it'd be an easy recommend, but with how abruptly the game ends I wish Steam had a Mixed or Neutral option. I'll still leave the game a positive review as I think it did more right than wrong but just be aware that this is a *very* short game that unfortunately doesn't quite stick the landing at the end.

I did enjoy The Operator, but it's very much one of those titles I wish I could give a sideways thumb to. I can't explain why without spoilers, so I'll tag that section.

This is one of those games that takes place entirely in menus, but still manages to have a compelling story with some puzzling that keeps you engaged in relatively simple game play systems by making you use the analytical parts of your brain. Taking place in a fictional early 1990s where people have cell phones and wireless Internet access, you're playing as a remote operator at the Not FBI who is tasked with helping field agents analyze data relevant to their cases. As you progress, you'll start to become embroiled in a huge conspiracy that goes through many elements of the agency and other places as well. The interface is nice, the music is good and the voice acting of the characters is actually great. If you like stuff that's more action focused, this might not be for you, but I was kept engaged throughout.

Non-specific spoilers and attached criticisms below:

[spoiler]Unfortunately, this game is really let down by it's in my opinion, pretty awful ending. Things come to a head very quickly and the conclusion is thrown at you over just a couple of minutes and isn't well paced. Things somehow manage to end on both a massive cliffhanger, but also very definitively, making the story unsatisfying and also not necessarily possible to continue in a sequel or expansion. You're introduced to some pretty cool investigative mechanics early on that only ever get used once and you also make many what seem like important choices, but you're given a very strong indication by the end that none of them ultimately mattered, nor impacted the outcome. People have said in the forums that there's little narrative value to additional playthroughs.

As a result, the story goes from intriguing and tense to being a big let down and feels like it was rushed and not fully planned out. This took an otherwise great experience and knocked a lot of wind out of its sails for me.

I still recommend this, but definitely on sale. I'm hoping that the developer puts out some content updates to expand the ending more, but I'm not expecting that.[/spoiler]

I gave it a thumb up although I'd have liked to give it a thumb "middle" if something like that existed on Steam. The reason is that while I loved the presentation, the music and the idea itself, it suffers from the same illness as 12 Minutes or Zero Time Dilemma: it starts great but the story gives you a plot twist just for the sake of having a plot twist at the end of the game. It looks cool and all while you're playing but as soon as the game is over... All I could think of was "what was the point of [b]THAT[/b]?"

I don't want to go into spoiler territory, so I won't say anything more about the story. It's reasonably priced and it's pretty entertaining all in all, even if the puzzles are not difficult. So that's why I think the game deserves a chance despite the story.

Finally, I want to add that I see some comparisons with Obra Dinn or The Case of the Golden Idol. Make no mistake: those two games are masterpieces. This one is pure entertainment. It feels like comparing Drive with Fast and Furious so to speak. For me, a better comparison would be the two titles that I mentioned at the beginning of the review where the surprise factor is more important than a coherent story.
